notes: Upstream entrypoint (/app/check-permissions.sh) only tests write access to DATA_DIR without requiring root privileges or su-exec. Compatible with Kubernetes runAsNonRoot: true and arbitrary non-root UIDs (e.g. 1000 or 10001). Ensure volume permissions (via fsGroup) permit write access to /app/data to avoid warning logs.

tunables.label: JWT Secret
tunables.description: Signing key for login sessions, WebSocket handshakes and CSRF tokens; required in production.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without it auth routes return errors and logins/WebSockets are rejected. Use a long random value and never rotate it casually — existing sessions become invalid.

tunables.label: API Key Secret
tunables.description: Key-encryption secret for issued API keys; required in production.
tunables.troubleshooting: The app errors on startup/key use when unset. Keep it stable or previously issued API keys stop validating.

tunables.label: Initial Password
tunables.description: Bootstrap password for the first management user on a fresh data directory.
tunables.troubleshooting: Only applied while setup is incomplete; after onboarding it is ignored. The example is a local-only dummy value.

tunables.label: Data Directory
tunables.description: Persistent data directory (SQLite database, keys, uploads); must point at the mounted volume.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep it on the declared /app/data volume, otherwise all state is lost when the container is recreated.

tunables.label: Server Port
tunables.description: Internal container listening port for the HTTP server; must match the published port target.
tunables.troubleshooting: If probes fail after changing this, update the compose mapping (for example 20129:20128) so both halves match.

tunables.label: Bind Address
tunables.description: Listen address for the HTTP server.
tunables.troubleshooting: Must be 0.0.0.0 inside a container; a loopback bind makes the published port unreachable.

tunables.label: Node Environment
tunables.description: Node.js execution mode; the image already defaults to production.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave at production — development mode disables caching and shows verbose error output.

tunables.label: Memory Budget
tunables.description: OmniRoute's own memory budget in megabytes.
tunables.troubleshooting: Raise together with NODE_OPTIONS (--max-old-space-size) and the container memory limit if the process is OOM-killed.

tunables.label: Node Options
tunables.description: V8 heap limit passed to the Node.js runtime.
tunables.troubleshooting: Increase alongside OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB when large catalogs trigger heap OOM crashes.

tunables.label: Migrations Directory
tunables.description: Directory holding database migrations applied at startup.
tunables.troubleshooting: Only override when migrations are mounted elsewhere; a wrong path makes startup fail to apply schema updates.

tunables.label: Require API Key
tunables.description: Enforce Bearer API key validation on all /v1/* endpoints.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep true for any non-loopback deployment — with the default false the anonymous /v1 LLM proxy is open to whoever can reach the port. Note it does not gate GET /v1/models (that follows dashboard login), so a 401 there is expected, not a failure.

tunables.label: Base Path
tunables.description: Sub-path prefix for hosting OmniRoute behind a reverse proxy prefix.
tunables.troubleshooting: In Docker the value is applied once at container start before Next.js boots, so it must be set on the first boot; also set NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the public origin including the same subpath, or dashboard links and API examples point at the wrong root.

tunables.label: Healthcheck Path
tunables.description: Custom healthcheck endpoint override (e.g. /healthz or deep probe /api/monitoring/health).
tunables.troubleshooting: Set it when OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH changes the effective URL, otherwise the health check probes a path that no longer exists and the container is reported unhealthy despite serving traffic.

tunables.label: CORS Allowed Origins
tunables.description: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for cross-origin browser clients.
tunables.troubleshooting: Only needed for browser clients on another origin — same-origin dashboard writes use session + CSRF and must not be fixed here. Exact origin strings (scheme + host, no trailing slash) are required or browsers reject the response.

tunables.label: CORS Origin (legacy)
tunables.description: Legacy single-origin CORS allowlist; upstream prefers CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS for new deployments.
tunables.troubleshooting: If both are set, prefer CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS — the legacy name only carries one origin and will drop additional front-ends. Never use CORS settings to patch same-origin dashboard 403/CSRF errors.

tunables.label: CORS Allow All
tunables.description: Development-only flag to allow any cross-origin browser request.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep false everywhere except local testing — true sends a wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so any website a user has open can call the API from their browser. It only takes effect after a container restart, and it does not fix same-origin dashboard 403/CSRF errors (those are session, not CORS).

tunables.label: Enable Pricing Sync
tunables.description: Enables background sync for latest provider pricing models.
tunables.troubleshooting: Requires outbound access to the pricing source; if the container has no egress the sync fails quietly and cost columns simply stay stale. Enable only when the dashboard is used for spend estimates.

tunables.label: Enable Models.dev Sync
tunables.description: Enables periodic sync with models.dev catalog.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set to false as a recovery lever when the dashboard is wedged on the same event loop and pricing sync cannot be toggled from the UI; re-enable afterwards to restore fresh pricing.

tunables.label: Storage Encryption Key
tunables.description: Custom key for encrypting persisted OAuth tokens in /app/data/server.env (auto-generated if unset).
tunables.troubleshooting: Set it before first boot and back up the key with the data — losing the key means the previously encrypted OAuth tokens in /app/data/server.env cannot be decrypted again; upstream auto-generates one there while it is unset. The example is a syntactically valid placeholder, not a real key.

notes: Health: GET / answers 307 (redirect to the dashboard) and GET /dashboard serves the UI; the image's own healthcheck script probes GET /healthz. GET / on the published host port doubles as the compose smoke test. Provider credentials are external requirements and are intentionally absent.
